title: Why Dominio de Valdepusa tastes the way it does

lede.text: Clay on top and pure limestone underneath: the two layers of one estate's soil each leave their mark on the glass.

chapters.title: One estate, one winery
paras: Dominio de Valdepusa is a pago, a single estate, in the municipality of Malpica de Tajo in Toledo. The vineyard covers 49.0848 hectares.
The wines are made in the winery on the property.

chapters.title: Hot summers, cold winters
paras: The climate is continental. Summers are dry and hot. Winters are cold. Day and night differ sharply.
The mean temperature is 17 °C in winter and 26 °C in summer. Rain averages 450 mm a year.

chapters.title: Clay over limestone
paras: A layer of clay 30 to 50 cm thick lies on top. Below it is fragmented limestone, 2 m or more deep.
The soil is basic (pH above 8). It has good structure and porosity, and it drains well.
The clay brings power and complexity to the wines, along with intensity. The pure limestone subsoil brings elegance and minerality. It gives the tannins a velvety texture.

chapters.title: Deep reds, aged in oak
paras: Only red wine is made here. It is very deep in colour.
Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon are the main grapes, with Graciano and Petit Verdot. The small amount of Merlot is made together with the Syrah.

Fermentation lasts at least 7 days, between 25 °C and 30 °C, with the grapes' natural yeasts. The juice macerates with the skins. The wine then goes through malolactic fermentation. It is filtered little or not at all before bottling.

At least 85 per cent of each wine ages in oak barrels of 225 to 500 litres. A single-grape wine needs at least 10 months. A blend needs at least 6 months. A blend made from already aged single-grape wines gets at least 6 more months.
